result.name: St. Mary Magdalene
patches: From the moment of that healing forward, Mary appears consistently among Jesus's most devoted followers — not one of the Twelve, but part of a wider circle of women disciples whose faithful presence the Gospels take care to record even when the male disciples' own courage occasionally faltered.

From the moment of that healing forward, Mary appears consistently among Jesus's most devoted followers. She was not one of the Twelve, but part of a wider circle of women disciples. The Gospels take care to record their faithful presence, even when the male disciples' own courage occasionally faltered.

Luke names Mary Magdalene alongside Joanna, wife of Herod's steward Chuza, and Susanna, among "many others" who provided for Jesus and the Twelve out of their own resources — a detail easy to pass over quickly, but one that reveals a genuine community of women disciples supporting Christ's public ministry financially and practically from very early on, a partnership the Gospels take pains to record even though the culture of the day rarely gave women's contributions such deliberate attention.

result.name: St. Andrew
patches: His feast, kept close to the beginning of Advent each year, fittingly reminds the whole Church, at the very start of a new liturgical year, that the entire Christian life begins with the same single, decisive step Andrew took by the Jordan: to leave what we know and follow.
